items.author: Katie Tarasov
items.highlights: As Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.'s Add To Watchlist record quarter makes clear, demand from chipmakers shows no sign of slowing down. The artificial intelligence boom has created unending need for space on factory lines at the world's leading chip manufacturer, and it could put a chokehold on the entire industry's ability to scale. Last year, TSMC said it had the capacity to make more than 17 million 12-inch equivalent wafers. But customers want more. ... items.author: Rexielyn Diaz
items.highlights: - TSMC stock is up 23% in 2026, but it has trailed AMD and Micron and is well below its October high after worries about AI spending hit chip stocks. - The business keeps beating its own plan: October revenue rose 59.7% to a record, and management now expects about 44% growth this year, up from about 30% in January. - Nvidia is widely reported to be TSMC’s biggest customer, and it reports on Nov. 17; margins and 2027 demand are the main risks. - The forward P/E is below its five-year average and 2027 earnings estimates are up since June, so the pullback looks like a chance to buy more. items.title: TSMC Reports Third Quarter EPS of NT$29.43
items.author: N/A
items.highlights: HSINCHU, Taiwan, R.O.C., Oct. 15, 2026 -- TSMC (TWSE: 2330, NYSE: TSM) today announced consolidated revenue of NT$1,494.24 billion, net income of NT$763.06 billion, and diluted earnings per share of NT$29.43 (US$4.60 per ADR unit) for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Year-over-year, third quarter revenue increased 50.9%, while net income and diluted EPS both increased 68.7%. Compared to second quarter 2026, third quarter results represented a 17.6% increase in revenue and an 8.0% increase in net income.
